diseases.name: Early Blight
diseases.description: A common fungal leaf disease that can reduce plant vigor and yield.
causes: Fungal spores in soil or crop debris
diseases.spread: Spores can move through splashing water, wind, tools, and infected debris.
immediate_steps: Remove heavily affected leaves with clean tools
treatment: Use crop-appropriate disease controls only as directed on product labels
Seek local extension advice for a crop-specific plan
organic: Use locally approved organic controls only according to label directions
avoid: Composting visibly diseased debris where it may survive
diseases.notes: This guide is general education, not a pesticide prescription.

conditions: Balanced water, airflow, and nutrition support healthy growth
immediate_steps: Check both leaf surfaces for pests

avoid: Applying treatments without a confirmed need

diseases.name: Late Blight
diseases.description: A fast-moving plant disease that can affect foliage and tubers in favorable weather.
symptoms: Pale growth near lesion edges in humid weather
causes: Pathogen introduction from infected plant material
diseases.spread: Can spread via wind-blown spores, rain, and infected plant material.
immediate_steps: Isolate suspected plants and avoid moving wet foliage
Contact a local agricultural extension service promptly
treatment: Follow qualified local crop-protection guidance and all product labels
organic: Remove and dispose of affected material according to local guidance
care: Keep records of symptoms and dates
diseases.notes: Severe or fast-spreading symptoms need local expert support.

diseases.name: Visible leaf damage — further assessment needed
diseases.description: The image contains substantial yellow, orange, or brown leaf tissue, so a healthy result would not be reliable. This check does not identify the exact cause.
symptoms: Yellow, orange, or brown leaf tissue visible in the photo
Possible dead, scorched, spotted, or discolored areas
causes: Pests, nutrient stress, watering problems, sun scorch, or chemical injury
diseases.spread: The cause is not confirmed. Avoid moving affected leaves or working with the plant while foliage is wet until you inspect it further.
immediate_steps: Check both sides of several leaves for insects, spots, and spreading patterns
Take a clear photo of the whole plant and note when symptoms started
Remove only fully dead leaves with clean tools if appropriate
treatment: Do not apply a pesticide or fertilizer based on this photo alone
Confirm the cause with a local agricultural extension service or qualified plant professional before treatment
organic: Water at the soil line and keep foliage dry where possible
Improve airflow and keep tools clean
avoid: Using unverified home remedies or treatments without identifying the cause
prevention: Monitor new leaves and nearby plants
care: Keep the plant in suitable light and spacing
diseases.notes: This is a safety result, not a diagnosis. A clear close-up plus a photo of the whole plant improves assessment.
